descriptionChirho: Noun denoting an ornamental head-covering, variously rendered as turban, headdress, or garland depending on context. Used literally of priestly headgear (Ex 39:28 'ornaments of linen turbans'; Ezek 44:18 'linen turbans'), women's fashionable headdresses (Isa 3:20 'the headdresses'), the mourner's turban to be removed in grief (Ezek 24:17,23 'your turban ... your turbans'), and figuratively as a crown of beauty given by God in exchange for mourning ashes (Isa 61:3 'a garland of beauty instead of ashes'; 61:10 'like a bridegroom adorns himself with a garland'). Multilingual glosses span 'turban/headdress/ornament/beauty': Arabic 'imama' (turban), Korean 'gwan' (crown), Spanish 'turbante/diadema'. The core semantic range is an ornamental head-covering used in worship, celebration, or as a figurative sign of divine favor.
